.
All Regional P.F.Commissioners
In-Charge of Regional/Sub RegionalOffices
Subject
Disposal of exemption applications pending for grant of
exemption under Section 17(1)(a) of the EPF& MP Act,
1952 and Para 27A of the Employees' Provident Funds
Scheme,1952and notification thereof.
Sir,
The Government
of India,
Ministry of Finance, with
a view to provide
legislative synergy between the Income Tax Act, 1961
and the Employees'
Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act,1952 and to tackle the problems
faced by the small investors in the recognized provident funds, brought out an
amendment in Rule 4 of Part A of Fourth Schedule to Income Tax Act, 1961
by
Clause 56 of the
Finance Act, 2006
so as to provide that
recognition to a
Provident Fund under the Income Tax Act shall be restricted to only such funds -
a) which are covered under sub section (3) or sub section (4) of Section
1 of the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions
Act, 1952; and
b) which
have been exempted
under Section
17 of the
Employees
Provident
Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 from the
operation of any scheme framed therein.
Page 1 of8

Page 2 of 8 
 
 
 
 
2. 
Accordingly, in Rule 3, after sub rule (1) the following proviso was inserted 
vide Finance Act, 2006, namely – 
  
 “Provided that in a case where recognition has been accorded to any provident 
fund on or before the 31st day of March, 2006 and such provident fund does not 
satisfy the conditions set out in clause (ea) of Rule 4, the recognition to such 
fund shall be withdrawn, if such fund does not satisfy, on or before the [ 31stth 
day of March, 2007], the conditions set out in the said clause and any other 
condition which the Board may, by rules specify, in this behalf: 
 
3. 
Consequent upon such amendment, sub rule (1) to Rule 3 to Fourth 
Schedule of Income Tax Act, 1961,  now reads as : 
 
“ The Chief Commissioner or Commissioner may accord recognition to any 
provident fund which, in his opinion, satisfies the conditions prescribed in Rule 4 
and the Rules made by the Board in this behalf, and may, at any time, withdraw 
such recognition if, in his opinion, the provident fund contravenes any of those 
conditions : 
Provided that in a case where recognition has been accorded to any provident 
fund on or before the 31st day of March, 2006 and such provident fund does not 
satisfy the conditions set out in clause (ea) of Rule 4, the recognition to such 
fund shall be withdrawn, if such fund does not satisfy, on or before the 31st day 
of March, 2007, the conditions set out in the said clause and any other condition 
which the Board may, by rules specify, in this behalf :” 
 
4. 
Further, in Rule 4, after clause (e), clause (ea) was inserted namely – 
 
“(ea) the fund shall be a fund of an establishment to which the provisions of sub-
section (3) of Section 1 of the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous 
Provisions Act, 1952 (19 of 1952) apply, and such establishment has been 
exempted under Section 17 of the said Act from the operation of all or any of the 
provisions of any Scheme referred to in that Section ;”

Page 3 of 8 
 
 
 
 
 
 
5. 
Subsequently, clause (ea) of Rule 4 was substituted vide Finance Act, 2007 
to read as under– 
 
“(ea)  the fund shall be a fund of an establishment to which the provisions of 
sub-section(3) of Section 1 of the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous 
Provisions Act, 1952 (19 of 1952) apply or of an establishment which has been 
notified by the Central  Provident Fund Commissioner under sub-section (4) of 
Section 1 of the said Act, and such establishment shall obtain exemption under 
Section 17 of the said Act from the operation of all or any  of the provisions of 
any Scheme referred to in that section;”  
 
6. 
The said time limit, which was initially for one year in the statute, has been 
extended year after year by the Finance Acts. The proviso to sub rule (1) to Rule 
3  was substituted by Finance Act,2012 which reads  as : 
 
“ Provided that in a case where recognition has been accorded to any provident 
fund on or before the 31st day of March, 2006 and such provident fund does not 
satisfy the conditions set out in clause (ea) of Rule 4, the recognition to such 
fund shall be withdrawn, if such fund does not satisfy, on or before the 31st day 
of March, 2013, the conditions set out in the said clause and any other condition 
which the Board may, by rules specify, in this behalf :” 
 
7. 
In view of the above amendments to Rule 3 and Rule 4 of Part A of the 
Fourth Schedule to the Income Tax Act, 1961, the EPFO was required to take 
necessary action in respect of the funds recognized under the Income Tax Act on 
or before 31st March 2006 and which do not satisfy the conditions stipulated in 
clause (ea) of Rule 4 of Part A of Fourth Schedule to the Income Tax Act, 1961. 
The time period given in the statute was initially for one year.  As the processing 
and finalization of all pending exemption proposals for forwarding  the same to  
Appropriate  Government  for  exemption through the Central Board of Trustees, 
Employees Provident Fund could not be completed within the period stipulated in 
the statute, it has been extended several times by legislative intervention vide 
Finance Acts of 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011 and 2012 on the request of EPFO 
forwarded to Ministry of Finance by Ministry of Labour and Employment, 
Government of India. The last cut off date to complete the task was 31st March, 
2013. Even then, the processing and finalization of all pending exemption 
proposals could not be completed by this target date.

Page 4 of 8 
 
 
 
 
8. 
The said time limit for satisfying the conditions laid out in clause (ea) of 
Rule 4 of Part A of the Fourth Schedule to the Income Tax Act, 1961 has been 
further extended till 31st March, 2014 vide Finance Act, 2013 and this is the last 
extension granted by Ministry of Finance for facilitating EPFO for taking necessary 
action in the matter.  
 
9. 
It is in this background, it has become necessary to concentrate on 
processing of all the exemption proposals, in respect of 295 establishments(list 
enclosed) pending in the field offices due to various reasons. The observations of 
Head Office in this regard are as under– 
a) In some cases, the establishments are still enjoying relaxation under Para 
79 of the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 and exemption 
proposals have not yet been forwarded to Head Office. 
b) In some other cases, proposals for relaxation/exemption submitted by the 
establishments have not yet been processed. 
c) Even in some cases, compliance to Head Office directions are still awaited.  
If the entire exercise is not completed by 31st March, 2014, no request for 
time beyond that will be considered in view of the deadline stipulated by Ministry 
of Finance, Government of India. 
 
10. 
In past, field offices had granted relaxation without forwarding the 
exemption proposal in complete shape to appropriate authority. As a result, 
establishments have been enjoying relaxation for years together and no steps 
were taken to process the exemption proposals pending for notification by 
Appropriate Government. 
 
11. 
It is observed that the exemption proposals are submitted by Regions to 
Head Office in a very casual way without proper verification of all check points, 
without analyzing the compliance audit reports and without all required 
documents. This results in unnecessary correspondence  with field offices and 
Ministry that consumes time also. While examining such cases Regional Provident 
Fund Commissioners In–charge of Regional/Sub Regional Offices shall state and 
certify as to whether the accounts of the establishment have been verified  for 
the period for which the establishment has maintained the Trust Funds before the 
date of  recommendations  and  the violations noticed thereof  are  rectified.  In a

Page 5 of 8 
 
 
 
 
majority of the  cases,  right  from  the  date of coverage, the establishment is 
maintaining the Trust and the contributions are transferred to Trust only.  Even in 
such cases, without attempting regularization of the period for which the 
contributions are not received in the respective field offices, proposals are 
forwarded for grant of exemption prospectively or retrospectively and for issue of 
notification. Regional Provident  Fund  Commissioners  In–charge  of 
Regional/Sub Regional Offices shall take steps to withdraw relaxation in cases 
where the establishments have failed to rectify the violations and shall take over 
the funds immediately. 
 
12. 
There are also instances wherein Regional Provident Fund Commissioners 
In–charge of Regional/Sub Regional Offices have recommended proposals for 
grant of exemption even though the Trusts have violated the mandatory 
conditions.  Once  the  Regional  Provident  Fund  Commissioners    In–charge  of  
Regional/Sub Regional Offices certify and confirm  that the Trustees of the 
establishment have rectified the violations and also made good deficiencies, 
which have been pointed out during  compliance audit, such cases can be 
considered on individual merits and appropriate recommendation be made to 
Head Office. Instances are also noticed that there exist substantial time lag 
between the date of coverage and the date from which exemption is sought and 
recommended and the date on which rules are approved. Henceforth Regional 
Provident Fund Commissioners In–charge of Regional/Sub Regional Offices  shall  
not permit  “deemed exemption” to  any establishment and shall incorporate a 
specific mention in the coverage memorandum so that in  case  any  
establishment, on  their  own, continue  to  maintain  the trust  funds  contrary  
to the instructions to comply as an un-exempted establishment and apply for 
exemption, the period between the date of coverage and date of grant of 
exemption will be considered as a default and all actions as provided under the 
Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act,1952 and the 
Schemes framed thereunder shall be initiated.  Such instruction will act as an 
deterrent to the establishment to commence compliance and not to rely on the 
tacit acceptance of compliance as an exempted establishment by omission.  
 
13. 
The exemption proposals need to be examined with reference to the 
essential conditions for grant of exemption and the conditions required to be 
satisfied after grant of exemption, as stipulated by the Central Board of Trustees, 
Employees’  Provident  Fund in their 176th  meeting held on 07.11.2006. The said

Page 6 of 8 
 
 
 
 
conditions are attached herewith as Annexure-I  and Annexure-II  for ready 
reference. It may be noted that the conditions as stated in Annexure-I and 
Annexure-II are required to be satisfied if exemption is sought retrospectively. 
 
14. 
Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India vide their letter 
No. S-35015/3/2007/SS-II dated 27.02.2007 has prescribed a 10 point check list 
(attached as Annexure-III) for processing and recommending exemption 
proposals to Appropriate Government through Central Board of Trustees, 
Employees Provident Fund. Before sending any proposal for grant of exemption, 
all the Regional Provident Fund Commissioners In-charge of Regional/Sub-
Regional offices shall ensure and certify that all the check points are met.  
 
15. 
In view of the above, all the Regional Provident Fund Commissioners In-
charge of Regional/Sub-Regional offices shall ensure completion of the processing 
of all proposals pending  in  their  offices  for  grant of  exemption  under Section 
17(1) or Para 27A after causing comprehensive compliance audit up to the 
Financial Year 2011-12 and complete the task by 31st October, 2013 without 
fail. It must be ensured that compliance audit reports are properly filled and 
completed by the audit team on careful verification/examination of all the 
relevant records as per the proforma already circulated by Head Office vide 
Circular no. C-II/Misc/02/06/Ex/EZ/26401 dated 28.07.2008 which is attached 
herewith as Annexure-IV. Further, all the Inspecting Officials shall be instructed 
to consult the employees’ trustees and employees’ unions during Compliance 
Audit and discuss various issues pertaining to the functioning of the Trust in 
accordance with the conditions stipulated in Appendix-A to Para 27AA of the 
Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme,1952 so that the interest of the workers are 
not jeopardized. This compliance audit shall not be mixed with the 
compliance audit of already exempted establishments for which 
instructions will be issued separately after completion of the exercise in 
question.  
 
16. 
The instructions issued by Head Office from time to time are appended 
below which provide clear guidelines about processing of exemption proposals 
and requirement of essential documents. 
 
a) 
C-II/Misc./2/08/Ex/EZ/65314-65429 
dated 
20.11.2006 
(circular 
enclosed).

Page 7 of 8 
 
 
 
 
b) 
C-II/MISC/2(06)/EX/EZ/88651 dated 09.03.2007(circular enclosed). 
c) 
C-II/Misc./2/06/Ex/EZ/79520-79690 
dated 
28.12.2007(circular 
enclosed). 
d) 
C-II/Misc./02/06/Ex./EZ/26401 dated 07.08.2008 (circular enclosed). 
e) 
C-II/Misc./2/06/Exem/Vol.I/5314-5464 dated 27.04.2009 (circular 
enclosed). 
 
17. 
All the Regional Provident Fund Commissioners In–charge of Regional/Sub 
Regional Offices are requested to ensure that the establishments seeking 
exemption fulfill all the provisions prescribed under the Employees’ Provident 
Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 and Schemes framed thereunder, 
confirm to the conditions incorporated in the Annexures and Circulars referred to 
above and satisfy all the requirements specified in the Compliance Audit 
Proforma. If from all such angles, Regional  Provident  Fund  Commissioners In–
charge of  Regional/Sub Regional Offices find that the cases are fit to be 
recommended, they shall forward the proposals along with all relevant 
documents and annexures as specified by Head Office in its Circular dated 
27.12.2007 referred to at sub para (c) to Para 16 above and after proper 
certification.  
 
18. 
Further during the compliance audit, if it emerges  that the establishment 
has willfully and persistently violated the condition of exemption or has otherwise 
attracted a condition for revocation of exemption/relaxation as prescribed in 
Appendix ‘A’ to Para 27AA of the Employees’ Provident Funds  Scheme, 1952  
(Gazette  Notification  is  attached  as  Annexure-V), Regional Provident Fund 
Commissioners In–charge of Regional/Sub Regional Offices shall immediately 
show cause the establishment/employer and the Board of Trustees as to why 
relaxation granted shall not be withdrawn. The show cause notice shall invariably 
be issued to the Employee Trustees also. After relaxation granted is withdrawn, 
all such cases shall be reported to Head Office. Further, in cases where 
recommendation of the Central Board of Trustees, EPF have been sent to 
Appropriate Government(Central/State) for further action, Regional Provident 
Fund Commissioners In–charge of Region  shall forward a copy of the order of 
withdrawal of relaxation to Head Office so that the matter will be taken up with 
the Appropriate Government for further action.

19.
Since Para 79B of the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme,1952 stipulates
that when an Appropriate Government consults the Central Board with regard to
its proposal for grant of exemption to an establishment under Section 17 of the
Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act,1952 and since the
Board is required to communicate
the views to the appropriate
Government
within a period of three months of
its receipt, any delay on the part of the
Regional
Provident
Fund
Commissioners In-charge
of
Regional/Sub Regional
Offices in not certifying and forwarding the cases for placing the same before the
Central Board of Trustees, EPF for consideration and before forwarding the same
to the Appropriate Governments will delay the processing of all pending proposals
within the target date fixed by Ministry of Finance, i.e. 31st March,2014.
20.
The entire exercise shall be completed by 31st October,
2013 and all the
pending proposals complete in all respects and fit for grant of exemption shall be
forwarded to Head Office latest by 15th November,
2013 for placing the same
before the Central Board of Trustees, EPF and for submission to Appropriate
Government thereafter. The work may be completed in a time-bound manner and
failure to forward the complete proposal within the time prescribed will be viewed
seriously.
Yours faithfully,
(P.K.
